messages:
maria: FYI I noticed a 18% drop in prefix-cache hit-rate on prod after the v2 key-hash change rolled last night. numbers from the perf-dashboard: p95 latency +12ms, token-cost +7%.
alan: likely candidate: we removed tenant namespace bytes to unify keys. any chance of cross-tenant collisions?
jeff: quick check: collision counts in cache-metrics show ~3 anomalous evictions/min on 3 tenants starting 02:14 UTC. could be hash truncation.
maria: repro steps: run `tools/cache-inspect --prefix 'conv:' --tenant T123` then diff keys across tenants. i found ~12 keys identical across tenants when using old sha1mod64 -> v2 truncated256.
anya: that matches a theory. v2 changed to siphash with 8 byte truncation for perf. short keys -> more accidental overlap.
alan: security concern: cross-tenant leakage even if payloads encrypted at rest, if we serve a cached KV from another tenant we could leak prompt prefixes or metadata. need immediate mitigation.
jeff: mitigation suggestions: 1) add explicit tenant namespace prefix to cache key (cheap) 2) HMAC keying per-tenant using KMS (stronger) 3) encrypt cache values and rotate keys.
maria: perf tradeoffs: namespacing is 0 CPU cost and small key size bump. HMAC adds crypto per write/read ~0.3ms on CPU-side; might impact hot-path.
alan: for compliance we'll want audit logs of cross-tenant hits + a plan to ensure no plaintext sharing. put a short incident label.
maria: quick patch proposal: rollback siphash-truncation -> restore previous full 32b key and add tenant prefix as immediate hotfix. then follow up with HMAC-per-tenant rollout behind feature flag.
jeff: can we do a canary on dedicated infra first? we'll route 5% traffic to a salted-key variant and collect false-positive collision metric.
anya: also recommend changing cache-key derivation to include model-id + prompt-version + tenant-id, explicit ordering. sample: ```key = f"t:{tenant_id}|m:{model_id}|v:{ver}|h:{sha256(prefix)}"```
maria: yep, that addresses both collision & future-proofing. also reduces chance of same prefix across different models hitting each other.
alan: for audit: add logging on cache MISS->HIT where tenant_id_mismatch flag set. store ephemeral stack traces and cached-key-hash (no plaintext prompt). keep logs for 30d.
jeff: rolling plan: 1) feature-flag tenant-prefix (hotfix) -> roll to 100% in 30m if metrics OK 2) enable salted HMAC behind feature flag for 5% canary 3) schedule full HMAC + key-rotation in 2 weeks.
maria: added runbook snippet for SRE: ```- detect: alert if cross_tenant_hit_rate > 0.1%
- mitigate: enable tenant-prefix FF immediately
- rollback: revert to previous key derivation if cache_latency > baseline + 50ms
- postmortem: collect sample keys and compute entropy/collision profile```
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started: rollout/tenant-prefix-hotfix -> canary. build #b-4876
anya: small profiling note: kernel-selection/batch behaviour also interacts: hotter batching means more reuse of KV cache; fixing keying will improve effective hit-rate more than kernel tweaks for this case.
alan: next steps for security: 1) brief compliance 2) record decision to encrypt values 3) rotate KMS keys for HMAC 4) add audit dashboard.
jeff: i'm on the rollback/hotfix PR, will ping here when the canary metrics land.
maria: thanks. if anyone sees unusual increased 5xx from runtime during canary ping now. I'll monitor hit-rate dashboards + per-tenant evictions.
jeff: canary metrics 10m in: collision count down to 0, hit-rate back to baseline, latency unchanged. promoting to 100%.
maria: marking incident as mitigated, will open follow-up ticket for HMAC + audit retention. :thumbsup:
alan: thanks team. we'll track compliance sign-off separately.
